Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No original source cited, so the claim could not be checked. National regulator ARCEP's Q3 2025 market observatory reports 39% of identified mobile terminals are 4G-capable and 1% 5G-capable (45% 2G, 15% 3G); GSMA Intelligence data via DataReportal shows 62-63.5% of connections are 3G/4G/5G ('broadband') as of 2025; a 2020 World Bank diagnostic put smartphone adoption at 40.9%. These proxies converge around the 40-59% band, so the original Value Code of 3 is confirmed, though no single source gives a precise device-type (smartphone vs feature phone) split for a recent year — recommend human review to pin down an exact current smartphone-specific figure.

Definition: The availability and presence of major cloud service providers (hyperscale and regional) operating in or serving the country with local or near-local infrastructure. Cloud availability determines access to scalable computing resources for government, business, and startups.
Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No original source cited. No AWS/Azure/GCP/Oracle region or availability zone exists in Togo; the country is served from distant regions (e.g. Europe or South Africa), consistent with Value Code 2. However, Togo's state-owned Lomé Data Centre (Tier III+, carrier-neutral, with a local IXP) signed an MoU in June 2026 with ST Digital to launch a 'sovereign' private cloud service hosted locally — this is a genuine local capability in the pipeline but was, at the time of the reporting (June 2026), still an announced partnership rather than a live service. Original code 2 is confirmed for now; recommend human review to check whether the SIN/ST Digital cloud has since gone live, which would justify moving to Code 3 or 4.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No original source cited and the <10% claim is not supported. World Bank data (sourced from IEA), the dedicated indicator for this metric, puts Togo's renewable electricity output at 25.30% of total electricity output in 2021 (most recent year available). Independent EIA-based generation data (via statbase.org) shows 0.1265 TWh renewable vs 0.5030 TWh fossil generation in 2024, i.e. roughly 20% of domestic generation — consistent in direction though slightly lower, likely reflecting Togo's heavy reliance on imported (often hydro) power alongside domestic thermal generation. Revised to Value Code 3 (25-49%) on the World Bank/IEA figure, noting the estimate sits close to the 2/3 band boundary — recommend human review to confirm the exact current-year split between domestic and imported generation.

Definition: The proportion of the population with basic digital skills (ability to use a computer, smartphone, or the internet for simple tasks such as sending messages, finding information, or using apps). Based on ITU household survey data, Afrobarometer, or national ICT surveys.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first.
revision_notes: No original source cited, and the <10% figure is not supported by any Afrobarometer or ITU data found. Afrobarometer's Togo-specific dispatch (AD361, fieldwork Dec 2020-Jan 2021) found 18% of Togolese own a computer, 32% have a phone that can access the internet, and 18% get information via the internet often. DataReportal/GSMA Intelligence data show Togo's internet usage rate reached 37% of the population by early 2025. No Togo-specific ITU household ICT-skills survey was found. Using internet use/access as the best available proxy for basic digital skills, revised to Value Code 3 (25-39%); flagged for human review given the absence of a direct skills-specific survey for Togo.
